title: Canonical derived evaluation for profinite internal functions
statement: For a normed field F in a universe containing all test parameters, let C_F be the all-continuous condensed ring [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and ordinary unbounded derived pushpull [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For a profinite P use the actual test X[P] with projection rho_P [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] and the existing free internal module C_F[P] [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Put D_P=R internalHom(C_F[P],-), derived in the second variable. Define beta_{X,P}:p_X^* D_P -> R(rho_P)_* p_{X[P]}^* as follows: pull the universal section corresponding to id_P to X[P], restrict along its actual diagonal X[P]->X[P][P], apply tensor-Hom evaluation and take its rho_P-adjunct, then right-derive this natural transformation using exact point pullback [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Evaluation is natural in the value module; this is the coherence used to assemble that transformation. Define parameter restriction by deriving precomposition with the covariant free-module map, and restriction of sections by the actual pullback adjunction unit followed by canonical derived composition. For an E-algebra F and E-module M, define M_F as the continuous-functions condensation [lem-sfb-topological-module-condensation] of F tensor_E M with its module topology. For finite-dimensional M and normed F this is exactly its finite product norm topology, without a completeness assumption. The condensation functor is chosen only from its full sectionwise universal characterization, which fixes the object up to the canonical isomorphism used by the supplied boundary identification. No invertibility of beta is built into this definition. The recorded monoidal module infrastructure of [lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions] is reused for compatibility with its existing scalar-restriction interface.
